Structure searches for rare earth (RE) hydrides of REHx (x = 1 - 12 and 13-24) with simulation cells ranging from one to four formula units were performed at 50, 100, 150, 200, 300, and 400 GPa. Our CALYPSO structural searches focus mainly on the REHx (x = 2-12) stoichiometries, Ab Initio Random Structure Searching (AIRSS) [10] calculations were also employed to confirm some of our key clathrate structures, while some H-richer stoichiometries REHx (x =13-24) were also considered in the AIRSS approach [10]. Each generation contained 50 structures, and structures in the first generation were produced randomly with symmetry constraints. All the generated structures are optimized to their local minima by using DFT calculations. Here, almost all geometrical optimization calculations are performed by using PAW potentials and VASP code [11]. There are two exceptions on La hydrides and Pr hydrides, where the geometrical optimizations are performed by OTF potentials and CASTEP code [12] since PAW potentials of La and Pr are invalid to be used at high pressure as tested. During structure evolution, 60% of structures in the first generation with lower enthalpies are selected to produce the structures in the next generation by PSO. 40% of the structures in the new generation are randomly generated. A structure fingerprinting technique of bond characterization matrix is applied to produce structures, so that identical structures are strictly forbidden. These procedures significantly enhance the diversity of structures, which is crucial for the searching efficiency of algorithm. The local optimizations are performed by use of the conjugate gradients method and the criteria of the enthalpy change is 2 \times 1 0 ^ { - 5 }   \mathrm { e V } per atom. For most of the cases, the structure searches reach the convergence after 50 generations covering about 2500 structures.

evidences.quote: Once we have the predicted structures at hand, we then optimized a number of low-enthalpy structures at a higher accuracy as a function of pressure using either VASP or CASTEP method. The plane wave basis set was constructed using the energy cutoff of 800 eV in all calculations, and the Brillouin zone was sampled with a k-point resolution of 2 \pi \times 0 . 0 3 ~ \mathring { \mathrm { A } } ^ { - 1 } . This usually gives total enthalpies well converged within ~ 1 meV/atom. The PAW potentials [13] are adopted for Sc, Y, Ce, and H in Sc-H, Y-H, and Ce-H systems for VASP calculations. While On The Fly (OTF) potentials are adopted for La, Pr and H in La-H and Pr-H systems for CASTEP calculations.
